claims.statement: O'Connor's 1994 formulation requires supervenience, nonstructurality and downward causal influence; it discusses hidden microproperties or dispositions as a rival explanation.
limitations: This supervenience commitment is explicitly repudiated in the 2005 model; do not merge the two dependence accounts.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: Kim's selected challenge allows ordinary downward causation but argues that a sufficient noncausal emergence base threatens to preempt the emergent as a cause; diachronic relocation alone does not remove this problem.
limitations: Original journal PDF not inspected; use reprint locators.
The argument has substantive assumptions about noncausal determination, sufficiency and exclusion.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: Kim treats phenomenal qualia as promising cases of irreducibility and recognizes novel powers of ordinary microstructural properties, so his challenge is not a claim that all qualia are already reduced or all whole-to-part influence is impossible.
limitations: No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: O'Connor and Wong's 2005 account posits basic nonstructural properties causally generated and sustained by organized physical systems, rejects general intrinsic synchronic supervenience, and explicitly repudiates the earlier 1994 supervenience formulation.
limitations: This is the authors' proposed ontology, not an established neural law.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: The 2005 reply treats the emergent as an intermediate cause in a temporal process rather than an independent redundant cause, rejecting the noncausal dependence premise of Kim's selected preemption argument.
limitations: Its original p. 32 cross-reference matches reprint p. 149 only at the passage level; no complete pagination map is asserted.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: The 2005 authors acknowledge a disputed simplicity comparison with latent microdispositional alternatives, offer a history-dependent thought experiment, and invoke contested first-person motivation; they do not supply an independently confirmed emergence law.
limitations: The thought experiment stipulates its discriminating conditions and excludes relevant physical probabilistic explanation by assumption.
The claim concerns what this paper establishes, not all evidence in the literature.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: Rejecting noncausal base determination and qualified physical completeness permits a distinct causal-chain response to the selected preemption argument; this blocks that conditional disproof without establishing that the revised ontology is actual.
alternative_explanations: A complete microphysical causal explanation may be available.
limitations: No general proof of metaphysical consistency or defeat of every causal-exclusion formulation.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: A fair comparison must count basic experiential properties, latent powers and laws, generation and maintenance conditions, and phenomenal-quality/subject assignments on each side; no selected original derives a uniquely confirmed theory from those costs.
alternative_explanations: Different realization or interventionist accounts not inspected here
limitations: A cost inventory is not a numerical parsimony measure or a winner ranking.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: If the 2005 ontology of basic nonstructural experiential property types is granted, strong emergence can satisfy a limited property-level reading of H-F despite causal dependence of instances; it does not entail a universal conscious ground or independent mental substance.
limitations: Conditional taxonomy, not acceptance of H-F.
Causal generation alone does not entail fundamental status; the additional nonstructural/basic-property premise does the work.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: The selected maintenance condition requires supporting organization; causal mental influence therefore does not establish H-B, and the model must reproduce inherited neural-dependence patterns and specify discriminating dynamics before empirical comparison.

source_locators.locator: pp. 665–668, especially p. 666 model and p. 676 note 11

limitations: No new empirical evidence reviewed here.
Does not prove consciousness impossible on every alternative substrate.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: The selected temporal emergence accounts do not by themselves establish H-U, H-S, H-T, H-P, H-I, H-G or H-A; property novelty does not supply a universal subject, same-person survival, timeless bearer, full preservation or moral authority.
limitations: No positive component upgrade; nonassessment does not mean equal probabilities.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: Shoemaker proposes micro-latent powers manifested in emergence-engendering combinations; even under this emergentism the complete microfacts fix macrofacts. He distinguishes causal power from mere nomic necessitation in his response to Kim.
limitations: The view is proposed conditionally; not evidence that actual microentities possess the stipulated powers.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: Shoemaker first discusses distinct physical and emergent microstructural properties, then prefers their identity under essential causal individuation, modifying the supervenience claim to concern descriptions or included states of affairs; he explicitly discusses but rejects a causal-base option.
limitations: The identity conclusion depends on his metaphysics of properties and laws, which this paper references rather than fully defends.
It is not equivalent to the nonstructural 2005 account.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

claims.statement: Shoemaker shows that a reply to Kim need not support the 2005 nonstructural ontology; deciding between them requires assessing causal property individuation, dependence and specified empirical discriminators, not simply counting successful replies to exclusion.
limitations: The 2005 paper discusses a relative of Shoemaker's picture; do not attribute every nuance of its opponent reconstruction to Shoemaker.
Later direct critiques of Shoemaker remain uninspected.
No empirical observation, posterior probability or independent replication follows from these philosophical texts.

arguments.name: Causally generated nonstructural experience
premises: Experiences have characteristics and causal relevance warranting explanation.
Organized physical systems causally support experience.
Experiential properties can be basic and nonstructural without being separate substances.
bridge_principles: Causal production does not by itself establish constitutive reduction.
Qualified causal completeness of an exclusively nonexperiential account is denied.
arguments.conclusion: A causal-emergent model is available as a distinct proposal; its actuality is not established.
arguments.strongest_objection: The complete microphysical causal story might explain all effects; first-person access may not reveal hidden constitution.
arguments.strongest_reply: Specify emergents as intermediate causes; compare latent-powers alternatives fairly.

arguments.name: Noncausal-base causal preemption
premises: An irreducible emergent has a sufficient basal condition.
Emergent influence must act through later basal conditions.
bridge_principles: A sufficient basal causal explanation preempts an independent irreducible causal competitor absent acceptable overdetermination.
arguments.conclusion: Emergent properties face causal and explanatory exclusion under the stated dependence assumptions.
arguments.strongest_objection: The base may act through an emergent causal intermediary, or mere necessitation may not bestow the relevant powers.
arguments.strongest_reply: The selected argument rules out a causal intermediary by its noncausal emergence premise; alternative dependence accounts need separate evaluation.
unresolved_issues: Justification and scope of noncausal-base premise

arguments.name: Temporal causal-chain reply
premises: Physical configuration generates and sustains an emergent over time.
The emergent mediates some later effects.
There is no independently complete parallel physical route in the model.
bridge_principles: Earlier causal dependence does not automatically eliminate intermediate causal relevance.
arguments.conclusion: Kim's selected preemption inference does not establish a contradiction in this revised model without its disputed premises.
arguments.strongest_objection: Relabeling the mechanism may add no explanatory benefit over latent microphysical powers.
arguments.strongest_reply: The authors contest simplicity and offer a history-dependent scenario; this motivates comparison without settling it.

arguments.name: Micro-latent powers and property individuation
arguments.position: Shoemaker countercase and reply to Kim
premises: Micro-latent powers manifest only in suitable combinations.
Complete microfacts, including those powers, fix macrofacts.
On the preferred view properties possess their individuating causal features essentially.
bridge_principles: Nomic necessitation alone need not constitute the relevant causal power in the provisional distinct-property account.
Under preferred individuation and noncausal dependence, equivalent causal properties are identical.
arguments.conclusion: A response to preemption can support a microstructural or descriptive account instead of basic nonstructural emergence.
arguments.strongest_objection: The individuation assumptions may be disputed; the 2005 model changes the dependence relation and contests the rival's simplicity.
arguments.strongest_reply: Shoemaker explicitly considers a causal-base option before rejecting it from his essential-powers commitments; the disagreement remains premise-dependent.
unresolved_issues: Latent-power laws unspecified for actual consciousness
